Audit logs: retention, format, access controls
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC tradeoffs for governance
Benchmarks: latency & token cost inside VPC
transcript: [00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we have about 55 minutes today to go over the governance items for the Nimble pilot. quick roll call?
[00:10] Marcus: Marcus here, hi. Priya?
[00:12] Priya: Priya Shah from SecOps, hi all.
[00:18] Leo: Leo, SRE. Aisha on legal will jump in for the contract bits.
[00:25] Samir: Great — Dana from infra will walk through the SSO flows and audit log hooks, and Elena will cover docs and next steps. Dana over to you.

[00:40] Dana: Cool. quick status: we finished the SAML metadata exchange on our side, we saw an error on the Nimble IdP assertion at first — looks like nameID format mismatch — that was fixed and we did a test sign-on yesterday from the staging tenant. we logged the assertion flows to the audit stream, but note that the log payload currently masks email fields by default per our hosted policy.
[01:05] Priya: can you repeat the masking bit? we need full subject identifiers in the audit trail for our compliance team for traceability.

[01:12] Dana: right, so: hosted default setting masks PII, but for Dedicated/Private you can configure unmasked subject identifiers and push to your secure syslog or cloud storage. in hosted we can also enable a config that writes full subjectID to an encrypted log bucket with shorter retention if you sign DPA addendum. there's a flag in the console called 'full_audit_mode' — might've been in the doc we sent but sorry if it wasn't clear.

[01:40] Priya: okay that matters. our compliance team wants 12 months of per-tenant audit events, exportable in json newline format and access controlled via SSO roles. can Redwood support that in the pilot?

[01:52] Dana: yes — for the pilot we can enable full_audit_mode in the private pilot deployment and route logs to your VPC S3 bucket via private endpoint. retention is configurable; we can set to 12 months. the only caveat is hosted environment has different default — if you remain hosted we'd need the DPA changes.
[02:10] Marcus: what about real-time alerting? we want anomalies on auth failures to flow into our SIEM.
[02:16] Dana: we publish audit events to a Kafka topic in the VPC or to your raw S3. from there you can attach Lambda or your SIEM forwarder. we'll provide a sample lambda in the runbook.
[02:30] Samir: quick question on SAML mapping: do we support groups -> roles mapping so we can limit access to production models?

[02:36] Dana: yes, we support attribute mappings and can map SAML groups into RBAC roles in the Redwood console. note there was a small issue with group claim size in some IdPs — if you have more than 200 groups you might see truncated claims, we have a workaround documented.
[03:00] Aisha: from a legal perspective, we need the SOC2 report and a summary of security controls. can you share your latest SOC 2 type II or the auditor's letter?

[03:10] Samir: absolutely. we'll share the SOC 2 summary and the compressed auditor letter. full report is usually shared under NDA — Elena will upload the summary and the list of controls mapped to our platform features.

[03:25] Elena: I'll put the SOC2 executive summary and the control mappings in the shared folder and flag the docs that require an NDA. also I'll include the incident response playbook excerpt and retention templates.

[03:40] Priya: retention templates are critical — specifically we want a per-tenant delete API or a way to purge test data within 24 hours after a user request. does Redwood offer per-tenant deletion?

[03:50] Dana: yes, the platform has a 'tenant purge' endpoint in Private and Dedicated modes that can delete embeddings and cached KV prefixes. on hosted we can run ad-hoc purges but there is an operational lead time. We'll include the API spec in the runbook.
[04:05] Marcus: any risk to cached KV (K-V cash) affecting purge? like if a token is cached will it survive the purge?

[04:12] Dana: good callout. caching is at the model serving layer — purge triggers background invalidation of KV entries; we can force immediate eviction but it may temporarily increase latency. we'll document expected window — typically under 10 seconds in Dedicated/Private, longer in hosted due to multi-tenant caches.
[04:35] Priya: on encryption: we require CMEK KMS integration and customer-managed keys for stored audit logs. supported?

[04:42] Dana: we support CMEK for Dedicated and Private. logs to S3 can be encrypted with your KMS. hosted tenants use Redwood-managed keys by default, but we can negotiate bring-your-own-key for enterprise contracts.
[05:00] Aisha: small ask: can you annotate the evidence for controls relevant to data retention and logging (CC6, etc) in a way we can hand to auditors?
[05:06] Elena: yes, we'll provide a control-to-artifact mapping sheet with screenshots, config flags, and sample log exports.

[05:20] Samir: switching to deployment mode tradeoffs: Nimble asked last week about cost/latency. if you need full audit trails and per-tenant deletion I'd recommend Private/VPC pilot to reduce friction. Dedicated could also work but we'd need separate GPU pools and slightly higher cost. does that align with your ops budget?
[05:38] Marcus: budget is tight; we'd prefer to start hosted if possible, but compliance might force Private. we need a clear delta in cost and a migration plan.

[05:48] Dana: we can provide a cost delta spreadsheet. also migration from hosted to Private is straightforward since models and routes are abstracted — you'll need network peering/endpoint setup and a short cutover window. we'll document steps and a rollback plan.

[06:05] Priya: about flagged redlines: we require retention policy that can be set per-tenant with minimum retention 30 days and maximum 12 months. we also demand immutable tamper-evident logs for 90 days. can you support immutability?
[06:16] Dana: yes — immutability can be enforced by writing logs to a WORM-enabled bucket in your cloud account, or using S3 object lock. Redwood's audit pipeline supports writing to that target.

[06:30] Leo: for the benchmarks — we need a small set of 3 representative prompts: short chat, long-context 4k prompt, and embedding generation. want these to be run inside our VPC to get accurate p95 latency. can Redwood help run them?

[06:40] Dana: yes, we'll run the microbenchmarks (p50/p95/p99) in your VPC during the pilot. Dana: propose to run them on 2026-07-01 morning in your region. I'll share the runbook and the exact curl commands.
[06:55] Marcus: last item — about audit access: who at Redwood can access raw logs? we want role separation and for access to require SSO and approval workflow.

[07:02] Samir: internal access is limited to named infra engineers with just-in-time elevated access and full audit for any access event. we'll provide the list of roles and the approval flow documentation.
[07:15] Priya: minor nit: sometimes transcripts we got earlier referenced 'Redwood Dedicaed' — just FYI the docs had a typo and it confused our procurement team.
[07:22] Samir: yup, thanks — we'll correct typos; the doc library will be cleaned up by Elena today.

[07:30] Dana: ok, to recap technical asks: 1) enable full audit mode and route logs to customer's VPC 2) provide SAML group->role mapping guide 3) tenant purge API spec 4) perform bench runs inside VPC. we'll deliver runbook and the sample lambda to forward logs.
[07:50] Marcus: good. any blockers on your side for enabling full audit mode in pilot?
[07:54] Dana: just the signed data handling addendum and confirmation of storage location. once we have that we can flip the flag.
[08:05] Aisha: legal will review the DPA addendum — I'll comment on the retention clauses by next Thursday.
[08:12] Elena: I'll prepare the shared folder with SOC2 summary, control mapping, the DPA template, and the benchmark runbook links. link will be in the calendar invite after call.

[08:25] Samir: timeline recap: Samir uploads SOC2 summary by 6/29; Elena uploads runbook and DPA template by 6/30; Dana runs benchmark in VPC on 7/1; legal review by Aisha 7/5. we plan to reconvene after bench results. does that work?
[08:40] Priya: yes, sounds good. one more: if bench p95 is over 300ms for long-context we may need model quantization recommendations. can Redwood propose quantization and batching knobs?
[08:48] Dana: yes we'll include recommended quantization profiles and batching settings given your prompt mix in the bench report.
[08:58] Marcus: ok thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity. any final questions?
[09:05] Priya: none from me, thanks.
[09:08] Aisha: none, thanks team.
[09:12] Samir: great — we'll follow up with the artifacts. meeting adjourned.
[55:00] Transcript end: automated notes: some speaker label noise present; timestamps approximate.
